concepts.def: Fletcher: do whatever love requires in each situation
Responsible care of God's creation and wealth
Giving a tenth of income to God / charity

walkthroughs.body_html:
Joseph Fletcher's situation ethics (1966): the only absolute rule is agape — selfless love.

In every situation, do whatever love requires — even if it breaks normal rules.

Strength: flexible and compassionate. Weakness: who decides what 'love' demands? Could justify almost anything.

Jesus: 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God' (Mark 10:25).

1 Timothy 6:10 — 'The love of money is the root of all kinds of evil.'

Christians teach stewardship — wealth is a gift to be shared. Many practise tithing (giving 10%) and support charities.

Christian Aid (founded 1945) tackles poverty in over 30 countries — disaster relief, fair trade, development.

CAFOD (1962) is the Catholic equivalent.

Jesus' parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10) and the Sheep and Goats (Matthew 25 — 'whatever you did for the least of these.') ground modern Christian charity.
